newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Philips Q1 profits rise 22 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Philips Q1 profits rise 22 percent.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday first-quarter ordinary net profit jumped 22 percent as its consumer products unit swung back into the plus column in what it described as a sustainable recovery.

Europe's biggest consumer electronics group said net profit from normal operations climbed to 460 million guilders ($239 million) from 377 million, with the removal of loss-making German unit Grundig from the operating results making a significant impact.
Investors cheered the figures, pushing the shares up 9.60 guilders to an all-time high of 100.70 in early business on a buoyant Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
Operating profit in the first quarter rose to 836 million guilders from 690 million, while sales pushed up three percent to 16.14 billion guilders.
"Grundig's out, that in itself makes for a significantly better picture," vice chairman Dudley Eustace told a results news conference.
But he added fundamental changes in the Sound & Vision unit, at the heart of the consumer products division, were also bearing fruit after the huge restructuring begun last year.
"The benefits of the purchasing programme, the cost reduction programme have shown through, whereby Sound & Vision has been able to outrun the price pressure by lower costs," he said.
"I have some confidence that this team has already made its mark on a more permanent basis, in creating a sustainable, profitable business," Eustace told reporters.
"The first-quarter results provide us with the confidence that we are on track following the improvement programme started in 1996," Philips said in a statement.
The Philips consumer products unit, which includes Grundig and Sound & Vision, turned in a 206 million guilder operating profit, reversing a 52 million guilder loss a year earlier.

The electronics giant said at the beginning of 1997 that it would no longer absorb 100 percent of Grundig's losses. Instead it would become a passive minority shareholder, booking Grundig's results under income from unconsolidated companies in proportion to Philips' 31.6 percent stake.

Eustace said talks with the Grundig family and Max Grundig Foundation were progressing slowly although he hoped there would be something to report by the time of Philips' second quarter results announcement scheduled for July.

Total first-quarter net profit mushroomed to 887 million guilders from a year-earlier 692 million, lifted by a 427 million guilder one-off gain from the partial flotation of Philips' stake in semiconductors equipment maker ASM Lithography.

However, Philips semiconductors, one of the main profit generators in recent years, saw operating income slip to 429 million guilders from a year-earlier 496 million. But Eustace told reporters he saw signs of a pick up.
Philips said sales had stagnated year-on-year, but added "this reflects an upward trend in performance compared with the fourth quarter of 1996."
Analysts' initial reactions to the ordinary net profit figure -- which came in well ahead of consensus expectations 366 million guilders -- were positive, albeit cautious.
"We are extremely pleased with this result and the progress that has been booked in this first quarter," ING Barings' Steven Vrolijk said.
But Delta Lloyd Bank's Peter Wortel was less upbeat. "Looking simply at the figures, it's good," he said. "Looking deeper...we had expected semiconductors to do better. In fact they're lower."
